clue.text: Smooth one's head of hair flatter

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: bland can mean smooth and unruffled in manner
one's read as 'one is', so I + S
the opening letter of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is told to smooth their hair to flatter their looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' looks like a verb about grooming, but it supplies an adjective; 'flatter' is the verb being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax with flattering words and pleasing compliments.

clue.text: Fastening to give way

blocks.note: first meaning: a clasp on a belt or shoe
second meaning: to collapse under pressure

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a fastener failing, but the two parts are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckle is a belt clasp, and to buckle is to bend or collapse under strain.

clue.text: Argue with Petruchio's stated objective

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so we want the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

blocks.note: in The Taming of the Shrew, Petruchio's aim is to change Kate's temper

explanation.surface: Someone disputes what a Shakespeare character was trying to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: Petruchio sets out to tame the shrewish Katherina, or Kate, so his aim is to alter Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to dispute angrily, a verb behind the noun altercation.

clue.text: Play receives award, making money

indicators.note: receiving something takes it in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a play is a drama
Companion of Honour, a British award abbreviated CH

explanation.surface: A stage show wins a prize and turns a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order awarded for service to the arts and public life.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the Greek currency unit before the euro, so it is money.

clue.text: Cut or burn enter hospital

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes into the other word, entering it

blocks.note: to sear is to scorch
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A first-aid instruction: with a cut or burn, go to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or cut off, as with wool or hair.

clue.text: Agent of influence

definitions.note: a factor is a thing of influence, a contributing element

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who acts or does business for another, such as an estate manager
second meaning: a circumstance that contributes to a result

explanation.surface: An agent of influence is a spy who sways opinion in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as one espionage term, but it splits into two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a commercial agent or Scottish estate steward, and also any element contributing to an outcome.

clue.text: One of five children, like St Thomas

blocks.note: one becomes the article a
a quin is one of quintuplets
as means like

explanation.surface: A child from a set of quintuplets is compared to a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Aquinas was the medieval theologian canonised as a saint and Doctor of the Church.

clue.text: Every player gets reprimand at half-time

indicators.note: taking half of a four-letter word leaves only its first two letters

blocks.note: tut is a sound of disapproval
the first half of time

explanation.surface: Every footballer gets a ticking-off in the dressing room at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the interval in a match; split, it says take half of the word time. In music, tutti means all instruments play together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for all performers to play at once, so every player is involved.

clue.text: Sovereign's assent to introduce a commemorative buttonhole

indicators.note: introducing one thing into another puts it inside

blocks.note: belonging to a sovereign is royal
OK is agreement
taken as written

explanation.surface: The monarch agrees to bring in a flower worn as a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside OK. Sprigs of oak were worn on Oak Apple Day, 29 May, to mark Charles II hiding in the Royal Oak.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal oak was a sprig of oak worn on Oak Apple Day to commemorate the Restoration.

clue.text: Working - as a boatman?

definitions.note: read literally: positioned on a river

blocks.note: first meaning: in operation, of a plant or system
second, playful meaning: afloat on the water

explanation.surface: Someone is asked if they're employed on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a literal reading of an industry phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plant comes on stream it starts operating, so the phrase means in production.

clue.text: Doctor cagey: I don't trust minor operation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are altered in order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A wary patient tells the doctor they don't trust a minor surgical procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'operation' both suggest surgery, but the operation here is a small business.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage industry is a small-scale business run from home, a minor commercial enterprise.

clue.text: A hound of staggering quality?

definitions.note: the article stays with the definition
read as one who lurches, a staggerer

blocks.note: first meaning: a crossbred dog used for poaching and coursing
second, whimsical meaning: someone who lurches about

explanation.surface: A dog is praised as being of astonishing quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' seems to mean amazing; the question mark signals it means reeling, giving one who lurches.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a cross between a greyhound and a working dog, so it is a type of hound.

clue.text: Illustrator of dodo had a hand in rejection of another bird

indicators.note: rejecting something turns it back, so the bird's name is written backwards
in bridge the four hands are compass points, so having a hand inside means one such letter is placed within

blocks.note: a small finch
East is one of the four bridge hands

explanation.surface: An artist who drew the dodo also contributed to turning away a different bird.
explanation.walkthrough: TENNIL is the linnet backwards, with E slipped in before the last letter. John Tenniel drew the original Alice in Wonderland pictures, which include the Dodo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Tenniel illustrated Lewis Carroll's Alice books, whose characters include the Dodo at the caucus race.

clue.text: Tortoiseshell cats - half of them run fast

indicators.note: keeping half of a four-letter word leaves just its first two letters

blocks.note: the front half of the word cats
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: Tortoiseshell cats are a breed, and half of them are said to race about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortoiseshell' looks like it describes the cats' colouring, but it is the definition: the actual shell of a tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise or crab, literally a tortoise's shell.

clue.text: Currency issued by French revolutionaries, since mark upset the army

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the word upside down, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: as can mean since or because
a sign is a mark
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, abbreviated TA

explanation.surface: French rebels printed money because their emblem had upset the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Assignats were paper notes issued in France during the 1790s, backed by seized church lands.

clue.text: Cuttlefish product is good in brine

indicators.note: one word goes inside another, sitting within the salt water

blocks.note: brine is a poetic name for the sea
PI, short for pious, is a crossword stand-in for good

explanation.surface: Ink from a cuttlefish is said to be good when kept in salt water.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a standard crossword abbreviation for good; 'is' only links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the brown ink secreted by cuttlefish, used historically as a pigment.

clue.text: Keep going through cold

blocks.note: per means by way of
severe weather is harsh and cold

explanation.surface: Carry on despite the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep going through' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends before 'through'.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to continue steadily despite difficulty.

clue.text: Having fallen, get a hiding in ringside classes

definitions.note: adjective: having fallen in social standing

indicators.note: something hiding in the words is concealed within them

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A boxer goes down and takes a beating in front of the ringside seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a hiding' sounds like a boxer's beating, which fits 'ringside', but it signals concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Déclassé describes someone who has lost social rank, fallen in status.

clue.text: Return, extremely emotional, to get shock therapy

definitions.note: verb: to return a candidate to office

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the end letters of emotional
electroconvulsive therapy, abbreviated ECT

explanation.surface: A very distressed patient comes back for electric shock treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' suggests coming back; here it means voting someone in, as voters return a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters elect or return a candidate when they choose them for office.

clue.text: Order off the list

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of place, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: all seven letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An item is to be ordered removed from the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it is a noun for a chivalric order. The Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is a Scottish order of chivalry, known simply by its flower.

clue.text: In a fox-hunting area, a representative plant

indicators.note: the words after are placed inside the area named, sitting within its bounds

blocks.note: the Shires are the English hunting counties of the Midlands
taken as written
a Member of Parliament represents a constituency

explanation.surface: Someone in hunting country, perhaps a delegate, is planted in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A and MP together sit within SHIRE. 'The Shires' is British shorthand for the fox-hunting counties such as Leicestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: Samphire is a fleshy coastal plant, eaten as a vegetable and growing on sea cliffs and salt marshes.

clue.text: Rider looking exhausted

blocks.note: first meaning: the author H. Rider ..., who wrote King Solomon's Mines
second meaning: gaunt and worn out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' reads as a horseman after a hard ride; it is the novelist's middle name, needing his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard means gaunt and drawn from fatigue, and Henry Rider Haggard was a Victorian adventure novelist.

clue.text: Big hole in Greek bowl

blocks.note: first meaning: a hollow made by an impact or volcano
second meaning: an ancient vessel for mixing wine with water

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as damage to a pot, but the two halves name one word in different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a large hollow in the ground, and also a wide ancient Greek wine-mixing vessel.

clue.text: Bird's mate about to fly

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word for mate is read backwards

blocks.note: a pal is a friend or mate
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: A bird's partner is getting ready to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' suggests a breeding partner of the bird, but it is just a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing is a crested plover of farmland, also called the peewit.

clue.text: Keeps asking what Nureyev danced in

blocks.note: first meaning: questions someone persistently for information
second meaning: light soft shoes, as worn in ballet

explanation.surface: Someone keeps enquiring about the ballet star's performances.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Nureyev was a famous ballet dancer, pointing to a dancer's light shoes rather than to a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to interrogate them repeatedly, and pumps are thin flexible slippers for dancing.

clue.text: Obsessive fear of bother with shoulder

blocks.note: to bug someone is to annoy them
to shoulder a burden is to bear it; 'with' just adds it on

explanation.surface: Someone has an irrational dread of trouble with their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent object of dread or annoyance, originally an imaginary goblin.

clue.text: Thrash son in rage

indicators.note: one letter is placed in another word, sitting within it

blocks.note: bate is an old British word for a fit of temper
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father beats his boy in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes after the second letter of BATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste someone is to beat or thrash them soundly, an old sense distinct from basting meat.

clue.text: Jew almost managed to get extra books in Bible - it's not quite clear

indicators.note: almost a whole word means it stops one letter short of complete

blocks.note: a Semite, a member of a people including Jews
ran a business means managed it
spare means surplus or extra
the New Testament, abbreviated NT

explanation.surface: A man gets more scripture from the Bible, but finds it hard to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of the first word is dropped. 'it's not quite clear' works as a definition by describing something partly see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something semitransparent lets some light through but is hazy, so it is only partly clear.

clue.text: Fail to finish oriental feast

indicators.note: not finishing a word means its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: oriental means from the east

explanation.surface: Diners can't finish an elaborate Asian banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oriental feast' reads as one dish, but the feast is a church festival on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a moveable feast of the Christian calendar celebrating the resurrection.

clue.text: Dunce's cap, say, for man getting a poor grade

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the word that follows is rearranged

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
taken as written, 'getting' joining it on
taken as written before the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A boy who scores a bad mark is made to wear the dunce's cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the dunce's cap as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce's cap is something worn on the head, an example of headgear.
